---
title: "Superstore Sales Performance 2023–2026"
output:
  flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:
    orientation: rows
    vertical_layout: scroll
    theme: flatly
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

library(flexdashboard)
library(DBI)
library(RSQLite)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
library(scales)

# The database built by R/01_load_data.R (one folder up from this file)
db_path <- "../superstore.db"
if (!file.exists(db_path)) stop("Run R/01_load_data.R first to create superstore.db")
con <- dbConnect(SQLite(), db_path)
q   <- function(sql) dbGetQuery(con, sql)

# Same colours as the Tableau dashboard
col_sales  <- "#4E79A7"   # blue
col_profit <- "#59A14F"   # green
col_loss   <- "#E15759"   # red

# KPI numbers (golden rule: SUM first, then divide)
kpi <- q("
  SELECT SUM(sales)               AS sales,
         SUM(profit)              AS profit,
         SUM(profit) / SUM(sales) AS margin,
         COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders
  FROM orders_enriched")

base_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_blank())
```

Row {data-height=120}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Total Sales

```{r}
valueBox(dollar(kpi$sales / 1e6, accuracy = 0.01, suffix = "M"), color = col_sales)
```

### Total Profit

```{r}
valueBox(dollar(kpi$profit / 1e3, accuracy = 0.1, suffix = "K"), color = col_profit)
```

### Profit Margin

```{r}
valueBox(percent(kpi$margin, accuracy = 0.1), color = "#76B7B2")
```

### Orders

```{r}
valueBox(comma(kpi$orders), color = "#9C755F")
```

Row {data-height=420}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Sales grew 51% from 2023 to 2026, peaking in the autumn months (blue = Sales, green = Profit)

```{r trend}
monthly <- q("
  SELECT order_month, SUM(sales) AS Sales, SUM(profit) AS Profit
  FROM orders_enriched
  GROUP BY order_month
  ORDER BY order_month")
monthly$order_month <- as.Date(monthly$order_month)

trend_long <- rbind(
  data.frame(month = monthly$order_month, measure = "Sales",  value = monthly$Sales),
  data.frame(month = monthly$order_month, measure = "Profit", value = monthly$Profit)
)

p <- ggplot(trend_long, aes(month, value, colour = measure, group = measure,
                            text = paste0(format(month, "%b %Y"), "<br>",
                                          measure, ": ", dollar(value, accuracy = 1)))) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Sales = col_sales, Profit = col_profit)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Sales & Profit ($)", colour = NULL) +
  base_theme

ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text") %>% layout(legend = list(orientation = "h", y = 1.1))
```

### Texas, Ohio, Pennsylvania and Illinois lose the most (US states)

```{r map}
state_profit <- q("
  SELECT state_province, SUM(sales) AS sales, SUM(profit) AS profit
  FROM orders_enriched
  WHERE country_region = 'United States'
  GROUP BY state_province")
state_profit$region <- tolower(state_profit$state_province)

us_map <- map_data("state") %>%
  left_join(state_profit, by = "region")

p <- ggplot(us_map, aes(long, lat, group = group, fill = profit,
                        text = paste0(state_province, "<br>Profit: ",
                                      dollar(profit, accuracy = 1)))) +
  geom_polygon(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = col_loss, mid = "#F2F2F2", high = col_profit,
                       midpoint = 0, labels = dollar, na.value = "grey90") +
  coord_fixed(1.3) +
  labs(fill = "Profit") +
  theme_void()

ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")
```

Row {data-height=460}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Tables, Bookcases and Supplies lose money

```{r subcat}
subcat <- q("
  SELECT sub_category, SUM(sales) AS sales, SUM(profit) AS profit,
         CASE WHEN SUM(profit) >= 0 THEN 'Profit' ELSE 'Loss' END AS profit_or_loss
  FROM orders_enriched
  GROUP BY sub_category")

p <- ggplot(subcat, aes(reorder(sub_category, profit), profit, fill = profit_or_loss,
                        text = paste0(sub_category,
                                      "<br>Sales: ",  dollar(sales,  accuracy = 1),
                                      "<br>Profit: ", dollar(profit, accuracy = 1),
                                      "<br>Margin: ", percent(profit / sales, accuracy = 0.1)))) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Profit = col_profit, Loss = col_loss), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Profit") +
  base_theme

ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text") %>% layout(showlegend = FALSE)
```

### Discounts above 20% turn sales into losses

```{r discount}
disc <- q("
  SELECT discount_band, SUM(sales) AS sales, SUM(profit) AS profit
  FROM orders_enriched
  GROUP BY discount_band")

disc$band <- factor(disc$discount_band,
                    levels = c("None", "Low (1-20%)", "Medium (21-40%)", "High (41-80%)"),
                    labels = c("None", "1-20%", "21-40%", "41-80%"))
disc$colour <- ifelse(disc$profit >= 0, "Profit", "Loss")

p <- ggplot(disc, aes(band, profit, fill = colour,
                      text = paste0(band, "<br>Profit: ", dollar(profit, accuracy = 1),
                                    "<br>Margin: ", percent(profit / sales, accuracy = 0.1)))) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey30") +
  geom_text(aes(label = dollar(profit, accuracy = 1),
                y = ifelse(profit >= 0, profit + 25000, profit - 25000)), size = 3.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Profit = col_profit, Loss = col_loss), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar) +
  labs(x = "Discount", y = NULL) +
  base_theme

ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text") %>% layout(showlegend = FALSE)
```

### Central Consumers & South Home Office are weakest (green = above 12.6% avg, red = below)

```{r heatmap}
heat <- q("
  SELECT region, segment, 100.0 * SUM(profit) / SUM(sales) AS margin_pct
  FROM orders_enriched
  GROUP BY region, segment")
heat$region <- factor(heat$region, levels = rev(c("Central", "East", "South", "West")))

p <- ggplot(heat, aes(segment, region, fill = margin_pct,
                      text = paste0(region, " · ", segment, "<br>Margin: ",
                                    round(margin_pct, 1), "%"))) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(margin_pct, 1), "%")), size = 4) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = col_loss, mid = "#F2F2F2", high = col_profit,
                       midpoint = 12.6, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  base_theme +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())

ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")
```

Row {data-height=110}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Key insight

- **Discounts above 20% lose money:** −\$136K in total; the 41–80% band loses \$77 for every \$100 sold.
- **Texas sells everything at a discount** (average 37% vs 7% in California) and is the biggest loss-making state.
- **Recommendation:** cap discounts at 20% and review pricing of Tables, Bookcases and Machines.
- Data: Sample – Superstore · Built with SQL (SQLite) and R (flexdashboard, ggplot2, plotly).
